findings.quote: For an eligible household, the full-month SNAP benefit is the maximum allotment minus 30% of SNAP net income, with that 30% rounded up.
findings.replacement: The base SNAP formula subtracts 30% of net income, rounded up, from the household maximum.
findings.defect: Qualify the raw formula as a base calculation; an otherwise eligible one- or two-person household can instead receive the $25 minimum.

findings.quote: A SNAP benefit equals the maximum monthly allotment for your household size minus 30% of your household's net income, with that 30% rounded up to the next whole dollar.
findings.replacement: The base SNAP benefit before any eligible minimum equals the maximum monthly allotment for your household size minus 30% of your household's net income, with that 30% rounded up to the next whole dollar.
findings.defect: Same base-formula versus minimum distinction; retain the existing detailed minimum explanation and correct tool behavior.
